findings.what: The in-line wiring reads ONLY `.regions` off the producer's envelope: `for (const region of produceOpeningTbRegions(regions).regions) regions.push(region);`. The envelope's `status`, `reason` and `refusals[]` — the named refusal D13.2 makes binding — are computed and then thrown away inside `normalizeAzureLayout`. Nothing persists them, so no downstream surface can ever show them. A trial balance the reader REFUSED is byte-indistinguishable from a document that is not a trial balance at all: both yield zero `opening_tb.line` regions, `readTieRegions` returns zero rows, and `parseOpeningTargets` answers 422 `{status:'unparseable', reason:'no_opening_tb_lines'}` (opening-parse.mjs:295-297). `isKeyedFallback` (opening-source.ts:53) then classifies that as the keyed-fallback signal and `opening-parse-action.tsx:109` renders it as `<StateBanner tone="info">` — an INFORMATION banner offering the keyed path. So a professional whose opening trial balance does not balance, or has one OCR-mangled row, is told 'this document has no trial-balance lines, key the balances instead' rather than 'trial balance does not balance: DR 130000.00 vs CR 129000.00' or '1 trial-balance row(s) did not parse: p1:y2.830(unrecognized_account_code)'. That is affirmatively misleading, not merely missing: it invites a person to hand-key a document whose printed figures the machine has just found to be internally inconsistent. The route's OTHER naming path (`namedUnparseableReason` at opening-parse.mjs:291) cannot cover for this — it fires only on regions that EXIST and fail `parseOpeningTbLine`, and every region the producer emits is re-parsed through that same function before emission (opening-tb-cells.mjs:210-213), so for the in-line lane that arm is effectively dead. The report's AC4 row claims all-or-nothing is 'proved three ways: producer refusals[] naming every failing row key, route 422 namedUnparseableReason, and p656.tie.fact_must_match counting zero rows'; the first never leaves the OCR function, the second is unreachable on this lane, and the third measures zero-rows, not naming.
findings.evidence:
MEASURED. Threw a red cell at packages/runtime/tests/zz-adversarial-656-refusal-leak.mjs (run on the rig with the worktree's own node, then deleted; `git status --porcelain` clean afterwards). It built three Azure `prebuilt-layout` payloads from the branch's own `kdoc-opening-tb-testkit.mjs` geometry and ran the real `normalizeAzureLayout`:
  CASE A — a TB short by RM 1,000.00: producer.status=refused, producer.reason="trial balance does not balance: DR 130000.00 vs CR 129000.00"; egress emitted 0 opening_tb.line regions; the egress OUTPUT carries the reason: FALSE; carries /refus/i anywhere: FALSE.
  CASE B — a TB with one unaccounted amount row: producer.status=refused, producer.reason="1 trial-balance row(s) did not parse: p1:y2.830(unrecognized_account_code)", producer.refusals=["p1:y2.830"]; egress emitted 0 regions; reason present in output: FALSE.
  CASE C — a printed GENERAL LEDGER (genuinely not a TB): producer.status=not_a_trial_balance; egress emitted 0 regions.
  A, B and C are IDENTICAL downstream: 0 regions each -> 422 no_opening_tb_lines -> tone="info". Verdict line printed by the cell: `Downstream (readTieRegions -> 0 rows -> 422 no_opening_tb_lines) sees A, B and C as IDENTICAL: true`.
The egress return shape is `{pageCount, vendorOpRef, envelope{schema_version,engine,content,pages,tables}, regions}` — there is no field the reason could have travelled in.
findings.fix: Carry the refusal, do not just suppress the rows. Minimal shape that keeps D13.1 (one in-line statement, one non-frozen module, no new lane): have `normalizeAzureLayout` keep the envelope — `const opening = produceOpeningTbRegions(regions)` — push `opening.regions` as today, and when `opening.status === 'refused'` emit the reason as evidence the consumer can read back. Two options, both inside the existing grammar: (a) one additional `field_path: 'opening_tb.refusal'` region carrying `opening.reason` as `text_content` (needs `opening_tb` already being a registered namespace — it is, 0191:554-573 — and `_derive_opening_region_fact` ignores any field_path that is not exactly `opening_tb.line`, 0017:1473-1476, so it is inert at the fact layer); or (b) put `{status, reason, refusals}` on the returned `envelope` (a free jsonb the writer already stores) and have `parseOpeningTargets` read it back in place of the bare `no_opening_tb_lines`. Either way `opening-parse.mjs` must split today's single 422: `no_opening_tb_lines` (tone=info, keyed path offered) stays for CASE C only, and a REFUSED read must answer with the producer's reason verbatim and render through the `tone="warning"` branch at opening-parse-action.tsx:113-123 that already exists and already prints the reason verbatim with the all-or-nothing sentence. Add a cell that pins A/B/C as three DIFFERENT outcomes — the red cell above is the shape.

AC6's owed evidence is 'the new walk at desktop AND 320px with an axe scan, a 200%-zoom leg, a keyboard-only path and a focus-return assertion' — those are legs 6 (:224 '320px + axe'), 7 (:242 '200% zoom'), 5 (:202 'keyboard alone + focus returns to its trigger') and 1 (:91 'the whole journey'), all fixme. Only leg 4 (:187, `?tab=opening` survives a reload / Back leaves the page) runs, and it asserts URL stability and one heading — nothing about the create dialog, the tie picker, provenance, the coverage footer, axe, zoom or focus. Worse for a reviewer: the author states at :52-54 that the failing assertion was never read ('The next pass should run the legs one at a time with `--reporter=line` and read the assertion, which this run never printed'), so the cause is UNKNOWN — it may be the spec's assertions, or it may be a real defect in the create dialog, and nothing in the branch distinguishes those. The one diagnosed fixture defect (the keyed-resolution read scoped by `bound_scope_id`) was fixed in the mock and, by the author's own note at :50-51, is NOT re-measured in the browser.
findings.evidence: Read the six `test.fixme(` declarations at the lines above and the one live `test(` at :187. The file's own header block at :29-35 records the measured run: `ok 4 (8.3s)` and `x 1 (12.2s) / x 2 (51.8s) / x 3 (54.2s) / x 5 (50.2s) / x 6 (50.3s) / x 7 (50.5s)` — every leg that opens the create dialog fails, and the ~50s timings are timeout-shaped, not assertion-shaped. 656-final.md's AC6 row concedes this ('partial — node cells done, browser proof RED'), so the gap is declared rather than hidden; it is still an AC6 that no browser proves.
findings.fix: Before merge, run the six legs one at a time with `--reporter=line` against the triple (`CLARA_E2E_APP_ORIGIN=https://127.0.0.1:3350 CLARA_E2E_NEXT_PORT=3351 CLARA_E2E_RUNTIME_PORT=3352`) and read the actual assertion. If the failure is in the spec or the mock, fix it and un-fixme. If the failure is in the app, that is a second finding and AC6 is not partial but red. findings.what: D13.3 rules `prior_gl`'s `business_operation` to `supported`. The migration does not do it: the A1 statement changes only `limits` and `basis` and leaves `business_operation = 'stored_only'`, and the file's tail at :506-513 then asserts registry-wide that no row reads `business_operation='supported'` with `typed_facts <> 'supported'` — i.e. it pins the ruling OUT from inside the migration. The author's justification is measured and, as far as I can check it, correct: `document-capability-registry.test.mjs:278-284` asserts that exact emptiness across all 240 rows, `0191:229-230` says the same in words, and `prior_gl.line` has never been produced — so obeying the ruling needs either a false `typed_facts` claim or the relaxation of a 240-row honesty law. But the branch nonetheless ships the registry's SECOND EVER publication with a binding ruling unfulfilled and a decision deferred to a report. The registry is the surface a professional reads to learn what Clara can do (`capability-tiers.tsx:72-79`); republishing it at version 2 with the level question open means the next republication has to be version 3 for one field.
findings.evidence: Read 0228:325-338 (`set limits = limits || '{"browser_entrance":"absent"}'::jsonb, basis = replace(...)` — no `business_operation` in the SET list) against DECISIONS §6.1 / brief-656.md D13.3 ('`prior_gl`'s and `opening_balance_doc`'s `business_operation` and `basis` are corrected'). Read the counter-law at 0228:506-513 and at packages/db/tests/document-capability-registry.test.mjs:278-284. 656-final.md Assumption 1 declares the deviation and says '**Orchestrator decision needed**'. MEASURED: the battery is green as shipped (31/31 on the rig), so the deviation is internally consistent — the conflict is with the ruling, not with the code.
findings.fix: This is an orchestrator call, not a worker fix, and it must be made before this migration merges, because the number it publishes is load-bearing. Three real options: (1) accept the hold, and amend D13.3 so the wave's record matches what shipped; (2) rule that `prior_gl`'s `typed_facts` also rises — but nothing produces a `prior_gl.line` region, so that would be the false claim 0191:217-218 forbids; (3) rule that the four-level vocabulary is wrong for this case (the migration header at :68-76 argues exactly this: `prior_gl` is 'read deterministically into human-ticked proposals, carrying no typed facts' and the registry has no cell for it) and file the vocabulary widening as its own ticket, leaving `stored_only` + the named `limits` as the honest interim. Option 3 is the one the measurement points at. Whichever is chosen, say so in DECISIONS before merge rather than after.

findings.where: packages/runtime/lib/opening-parse.mjs:236-238 (the new arm) proved by packages/runtime/tests/wave-b-opening-parse.test.mjs:295-320 (raw INSERTs at :296 and :304)
findings.what: The branch adds a new production refusal — CLR10 with message `op_key reused with different args` is reclassified from 422 `malformed_lines` to 409 `{status:'conflict', reason:'source_reread_since_parse'}` — and the only cell that exercises it builds its second extraction and its `opening_tb.line` regions with RAW INSERTs straight into `clara.document_extractions` and `clara.document_regions`, bypassing `clara.persist_document_extraction` and therefore bypassing `_derive_opening_region_fact`'s monetary corroboration (0017:1494-1499) and `_assert_field_path` (0191:554). That is precisely the fixture rule this branch adopted pre-emptively from #857 and wrote down as a rule in its own docs. The material consequence is not style: over the REAL path the branch's own DB battery measures a DIFFERENT outcome. `p656.tie.stale_extraction` (opening-ledger-source.test.mjs:371-400) re-runs the producer through the real `persist_document_extraction` and gets `stale_extraction_version` / `extraction_not_accepted` (CLR31 -> a typed 409 `refused`), not the new CLR10 `source_reread_since_parse`. Which refusal a genuine re-OCR actually produces — the CLR10 op-key collision the new arm names, or a CLR31 staleness refusal reached first — is therefore unmeasured, and the successor contract in 656-final.md already promises Clara the `source_reread_since_parse` string as a mapped refusal.
findings.evidence: `git diff origin/main...HEAD` adds exactly one `insert into clara.document_regions` (the branch adds it at wave-b-opening-parse.test.mjs:304; `git show origin/main:...` shows the file previously had one, at :148, so the pattern is pre-existing in that file but the NEW cell propagates it). The extraction row is likewise hand-inserted at :296 (`insert into clara.document_extractions(... engine_id,'rig-ocr:2' ...) returning id`). The branch's own stated rule is at packages/db/tests/README.md:313-314: 'Every `opening_tb.line` region fixture is created through `clara.persist_document_extraction` (#857's rule, adopted early). A raw INSERT would let a cell prove the database accepts evidence the...'. The DB battery obeys it (opening-ledger-source.test.mjs:134-152 goes through `clara.persist_document_extraction`) and so does the World leg. MEASURED: I ran the World leg on the rig — `node tests/opening-ledger-source-e2e.mjs` -> `PASS — producer -> persist -> cite -> approve, end to end, on real Postgres under real roles`, 5 regions, 5 targets, 5 approvals, `trial_balance_as_of` cent-for-cent — so the real path works; it is the RE-READ path that is only synthetic. FAILED REFUTATION worth recording: I expected the `op_key reused with different args` discriminator to be an unpinned free-text match, and it is not — migrations 0043:5029 and 0044:5712 both `raise` when that literal is absent from `_reserve_op`'s source, so the string is pinned twice.
findings.fix: Rebuild the re-read cell on the real writer: re-run `produceTbRegions`-style persistence (a second real `clara.persist_document_extraction` call on a second real OCR task) instead of the two raw INSERTs, then call `parseOpeningTargets` twice through `openingOpKey` and assert which refusal actually arrives. If it turns out to be CLR31 staleness rather than CLR10, the new arm at opening-parse.mjs:236-238 is dead code on the real path and the successor contract's `source_reread_since_parse` mapping must be withdrawn; if it is CLR10, the cell now proves it. Either way the measurement is cheap — the DB battery already has the whole fixture kit.

findings.what: The wiring is kind-blind by ruling (D13.1) and the module's header accepts that, arguing the worst case is 'a few extra evidence rows on a document nobody ever ties'. That understates the blast radius by one step. `_derive_opening_region_fact` does not merely ignore a bad `opening_tb.line` region — it RAISES CLR31 (`opening_extraction_evidence_malformed` when `amount_cents <= 0` or the side is null, `opening_extraction_monetary_mismatch` when the supplied `monetary_cents` disagrees with the text it re-derives), and it is called from inside `clara.persist_document_extraction`'s region loop at 0017:1587. A raise there aborts the WHOLE persist, so the entire OCR extraction of that document is lost — including a payslip's or an invoice's own regions. Before this branch no production caller emitted an `opening_tb.line` region at all, so that abort was structurally unreachable; it is now reachable on every azure-di layout pass, for every document kind, in every firm. The module's 'IT NEVER THROWS' containment (opening-tb-produce.mjs:110-112) is a JS try/catch and covers none of this, because the raise is on the database side one call later.
findings.evidence: Read 0017:1488-1499 (the two `raise exception ... using errcode='CLR31'` arms) and 0017:1587 (`select * into v_derived from clara._derive_opening_region_fact(...)` inside the persist loop). FAILED REFUTATION, stated plainly: I could not construct an input that reaches it. `_assert_field_path` (0191:554-573) is kind-agnostic and registers `opening_tb`, so no namespace refusal. A text the DB regexp does not match returns early without raising (0017:1476), so a non-matching emission is inert. A zero-amount row never becomes a line (`nilRow`, opening-tb-cells.mjs:370-374). And the producer re-parses every emitted line through `parseOpeningTbLine` and requires the identical triple before emission (opening-tb-cells.mjs:210-213), so a JS/plpgsql arithmetic divergence — `parseOpeningTbLine:45-48` does `ringgit * 100 + sen` in IEEE double with `Number.isSafeInteger` checked on the OPERANDS but not the product, while the DB does it in `bigint` — fails CLOSED, as a refusal to emit, not as a bad emission. MEASURED that existing OCR behaviour is unperturbed: `node --test tests/f4-egress-release-hold.test.mjs tests/intake-egress.test.mjs` -> 8/8 pass including 'Azure layout normalization keeps page-polygon provenance'; the only red was `f-a1-witness-egress.test.mjs`, which is an `ECONNREFUSED ::1:5432` from a missing PG env, not a branch defect. So this is a real widening of the failure surface with no demonstrated trigger.
findings.fix: Cheap belt for a hot path: since `produceOpeningTbRegions` already re-derives each line, also refuse to emit any region whose `monetary_cents` string does not equal the BigInt it derived, and drop the whole set (not the line) if any does — the all-or-nothing law already there, applied one layer lower. Alternatively assert the invariant in a cell: persist a deliberately contradicting `opening_tb.line` region through `clara.persist_document_extraction` and pin that the WHOLE call aborts, so the next person who touches `toRegion` learns what it costs. Neither is a merge blocker; the note is that the module's own header should say 'a bad region costs the document its whole extraction', not 'a few extra evidence rows'.

findings.what: Two cells pin their refusal with a disjunction over two different tokens — `assert.ok(["stale_extraction_version", "extraction_not_accepted"].includes(claraReason(err)))` — so neither `p656.tie.stale_extraction` nor `p656.tie.approve_rebinds` records WHICH wall fired. Those are two materially different facts: `stale_extraction_version` means `documents.authoritative_extraction_id` points elsewhere (0017:1723-1726), `extraction_not_accepted` means the run's own `status <> 'done'` or it is superseded. A future change that swaps one for the other passes both cells silently, and the report cites them as the evidence for AC2's `p656.tie.fact_must_match` family.
findings.evidence: Read at :385 and :440. Both cells pass on the rig (31/31 measured above), so the looseness is not currently masking a failure — it is masking which of two mechanisms is doing the work.
findings.fix: Assert the one token each fixture actually produces, and if it genuinely varies by timing, split the cell so each arm has its own deterministic fixture. A disjunction is the right shape only when both outcomes are equally correct, and here they are not — they describe different walls.

findings.what: The helper is documented as 'ONE producer run: persist `lines` as `opening_tb.line` regions through the real writer, in exactly the element shape `packages/runtime/lib/opening-tb-cells.mjs`'s `toRegion` emits'. It does go through the real DB writer — which is the part that matters and which A5 credits it for — but it hand-builds the region payload rather than calling `toRegion` / `produceOpeningTbRegions`. So every `p656.tie.*` cell proves the DB's behaviour over a HAND-WRITTEN mirror of the producer's output, and if `toRegion` drifts (a locator key, the `monetary_cents` string form, the canonical text) the whole `p656.tie.*` family stays green while production breaks. The single place the real producer's bytes meet the real writer is the World leg.
findings.evidence: Read :141-151 — the `regions` array is a literal object built in the test (`locator_kind`, `locator`, `field_path: "opening_tb.line"`, `text_content: tbRegionText(l)`, `monetary_raw`, `monetary_cents: String(...)`) with no import from `opening-tb-cells.mjs` or `opening-tb-produce.mjs`. MEASURED: the World leg does close the gap — `packages/runtime/tests/opening-ledger-source-e2e.mjs` ran green on the rig and logged 'producer emitted 5 opening_tb.line regions in line' then 'persisted 5 regions on the authoritative extraction, every triple re-derived'. So the coverage exists; it exists in ONE file, not in the twelve-cell battery that names the producer.
findings.fix: Import `produceOpeningTbRegions` in the DB battery and build `regions` from it (feeding it the testkit's `tables.*` shape, as `opening-tb-produce.test.mjs` already does), so a `toRegion` drift reds twelve cells instead of one. If a cross-package import is unwanted in `packages/db/tests`, at minimum assert in `opening-tb-produce.test.mjs` that `toRegion`'s key set equals the literal this helper writes.

findings.what: Recorded so the next reviewer does not re-spend the time. Seven attacks I tried and could NOT land. (1) SILENT NO-OP REPUBLICATION: `prior_gl`'s basis is corrected with `replace(basis, '<exact sentence>', ...)`, which returns the string unchanged if the sentence is absent — but the tail catches it, asserting at 0228:487-495 that the corrected rows now contain `create_seeding_batch` and `/api/seeding/prepare` and no longer contain 'Clara derives nothing to drive it'. (2) RE-BASED CELLS MADE VACUOUS: the registry battery's re-basing uses a LITERAL `const PUBLISHED_REGISTRY_VERSION = 2` (document-capability-registry.test.mjs:76) with the reason written beside it, not a value read back from the table, so the assertions stay meaningful; the 5->3 downgrade probe is untouched. (3) PINS THAT WOULD NOT MATCH A FROM-SCRATCH CHAIN: none of the thirteen pinned bodies is declared as a recut by 0225 (#655), 0226 (#657) or 0227 (#651) in DECISIONS §2 — 0226's 'thirteen cores' are 0129's BANK agent cores, not the opening lane — and the pin comparison is fail-closed (`is distinct from` -> `raise ... errcode='CLR10'`), which is the correct posture. (4) A DEAD TEXT-MATCH DISCRIMINATOR: the `op_key reused with different args` match at opening-parse.mjs:236 is pinned twice in the estate (0043:5029, 0044:5712). (5) AN UNSAFE TIE PICKER: `TIE_DOCUMENT_KINDS` (opening-source.ts:194) is exactly `['opening_balance_doc','management_account']` — `prior_gl` is correctly excluded, matching create_opening_seed's CLR02 at 0017:2913-2917 — and rows with `bytes_verified_at === null` are dropped at :227. (6) A BROKEN OCR PATH: the existing normalization tests stay green (see A6's evidence).
